claims.statement: The overlay mount request for workload demo-01 specified upperdir=/state/upper and workdir=/scratch/work on different filesystem mounts.
/state/upper resides on an ext4 filesystem (mount_id 41) while /scratch/work resides on a tmpfs filesystem (mount_id 52), so they are not under the same mount.
The kernel rejected the overlay mount with EINVAL, logging 'overlayfs: workdir and upperdir must reside under the same mount'.
The overlay mount failure (EINVAL) is the primary cause of the container failing to start: root filesystem preparation failed, so container init never started.
The StartupController readiness timeout is a downstream consequence of the container init never starting, not an independent failure.
The 'background connectivity probe delayed' event from NetworkMonitor is unrelated to the startup failure and is a candidate for incidental noise.

evidence_gaps.question: Why were upperdir and workdir configured on different mounts?
missing_evidence: Container runtime / storage driver configuration that generated the overlay mount options
Any prior mount setup or volume provisioning logs for /state and /scratch

evidence_gaps.question: Is the cross-source ordering between the kmsg overlayfs error and the logcat EINVAL error definitively established?
missing_evidence: A shared monotonic timestamp correlating the kmsg event (monotonic 620.15) with the logcat events

recommended_next_checks: Inspect the container runtime / storage driver configuration to confirm why upperdir and workdir were placed on different mounts (ext4 vs tmpfs).
Verify the intended overlay mount layout: workdir should be a subdirectory of the same filesystem as upperdir.
Review volume provisioning for /state and /scratch to determine whether /scratch/work was incorrectly mounted as a separate tmpfs.
Confirm the kmsg overlayfs error correlates to the same mount attempt via monotonic timestamps.
